item.title: Noah Kahan Clears Up Commonly Misheard Lyrics That Aren’t Nearly as NSFW as Fans Think
item.description:
Here's a short and engaging podcast script based on the article:
[INTRO MUSIC]
Host: Welcome to "Trending on Billboard"! Today, we're talking about singer-songwriter Noah Kahan and a hilarious public service announcement he recently shared with his fans.
[SHORT MUSIC TRANSITION]
Host: It turns out that some of Kahan's fans have been mishearing his lyrics, and he decided to set the record straight. He took to social media to share "some lyric clarifications" from his songs. For example, in his breakout single "Stick Season", the lyric is actually "Saw your mom", not "Suck Your Mom".
[SHORT MUSIC TRANSITION]
Host: He also cleared up a few more misconceptions, like in his song "23", the line is "Beat your ass into morning", not "Eat Your Ass In The Morning". And in his track "Haircut", the correct lyric is "Glad you got your act cleaned", not "Glad You Got Your Ass cleaned".
[SHORT MUSIC TRANSITION]
Host: Kahan's been on tour lately, and it's likely that he heard these misheard lyrics from fans at his shows. But don't worry, he's not judging – in fact, he gave his fans permission to "sing from whatever place your mind takes you". However, he did have to issue a separate PSA recently, reminding fans to please use the bathroom facilities at his shows... for everyone's sake.
[OUTRO MUSIC]
Host: That's it for today's episode of "Trending on Billboard". Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next one!
[OUTRO MUSIC CONTINUES]
